caption:
A mortar shell landed 1.5 metres from him in the Kargil War. Gangrene took his leg. He taught himself to run on a blade instead.

Major D.P. Singh was a serving Indian Army officer during the 1999 Kargil War when a mortar shell landed within 1.5 metres of him, tearing through his body with shrapnel. His right leg later developed gangrene and had to be amputated. Rather than ending his active life, he taught himself to run again on a prosthetic blade. In 2011 he became the first Indian to complete a marathon on a blade prosthesis, going on to run in 26+ half-marathons, including three at extreme high altitude near Leh, at roughly 11,700 feet. In 2019 he became the first Indian amputee to skydive solo. The Limca Book of Records named him to its 'People of the Year' list in 2016 and he now works as a motivational speaker, encouraging other amputees to compete rather than stop.
